text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israel braces for more attacks after Wednesday's suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market.
- U.S. Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich takes tough line on Palestinians.
- Arab League to hold extraordinary meeting in Cairo on Tuesday to discuss "Israeli oppressive practices" against Palestinians.
- Iranian President-elect Mohammad Khatami starts term by stressing Iran's principles and policies.
- U.N. monitors to be stationed at Iraqi border post al-Walid to import goods from Syria. Baghdad to take part in Damascus international trade fair.
- Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) sealed deals for fertilisers worth $54.5 million with 11 foreign companies.
- British Foreign Ministry source says Britain will send envoy to Middle East next week to seek revival of peace process.

- Contracts of Arab Establishment for Investments Insurance in first half of 1997 total $37.1 million. Syria's total benefit of insurance operation was $34.2 million until end of 1996. Establishment insurance operations were worth $1.3 billion until end of 1996 and included all Arab countries. Saudi Arabia had biggest share of $20.9 million in export insurance contracts, followed by Lebanon with $6.5 million.
